user_scenario:
You are Marisol Pereira, a retired county librarian in Poulsbo who pays the household's dental premium once a year and likes to get it done early and correctly. You are calling, unhurried and friendly but precise, because the check you mailed on November 18 for next year's renewal came back: you wrote it on the old joint checking account you and Daniel had just closed. You want to pay next year now, by card, yourself, so it is off your list before the holidays. You and your husband Daniel also applied this week, on December 2, for a Cascade vision plan to start on January 1, and you want the payment you make today to cover that too, so the vision plan starts on time. You would like the agent to work out the right amount for next year.

To be found you give your phone number, 3605550177. To confirm who you are you give your date of birth, March 9, 1974 (1974-03-09), and your ZIP code, 98370; other details only if asked again. Your member ID, if asked, is CMD7455027. You do not know internal account numbers and expect the agent to look them up. You remember the renewal notice shows $1,656.23, the same as last year, but you would rather the agent tell you what to pay.

If the agent asks who the vision plan is for, you say it is just for you and Daniel. If the agent asks about your son Gabriel or anyone leaving the plan, you say Gabriel turned 26 last November and came off your dental plan at the end of that month, together with his orthodontic rider, which he never got to use; you do not bring Gabriel up yourself. If the agent asks about the returned check, you confirm it and say the bank's notice also mentioned a fee. If the agent explains that something on the account has to be corrected or credited before next year's amount can be settled, you say that is fine and to go ahead.

When the agent tells you the amount to pay for next year, you ask once what it includes, accept the explanation and do not offer a figure of your own. When the agent gives you the payment step to complete yourself, you complete it with the account reference and the exact amount the agent gives you, paying by card. When you see the card confirmation, you read the confirmation number back once, thank the agent and say goodbye. You do not ask for anything else: no refund, no change to how you pay, no new plan or rider, and nothing to be mailed.
